description:
kith-store/src/lib.rs has a migration runner (Store::migrate) that applies migrations sequentially by comparing PRAGMA user_version to each migration's target version. Two design choices here are worth defending:

1. RAW_MIGRATIONS set (line 774): SQLite silently ignores PRAGMA foreign_keys changes inside a multi-statement transaction. V16 needed to disable FK enforcement to recreate the messages table with a cascade FK. The runner detects whether a migration is in the RAW_MIGRATIONS set and runs it outside a transaction. This is documented and correct; the alternative (silently ignoring the FK toggle and leaving cascade enforcement broken) would be a silent data integrity bug.

2. Single snapshot of user_version before the loop: the runner reads user_version once at the start and compares it against migration version numbers in the loop. The comment (line 762-768) explains why this is safe: migrations are strictly additive and ordered, and kithd is single-writer. This avoids re-reading user_version on each iteration (which would be unnecessary and could mask bugs in a theoretical concurrent-writer scenario).

Both are non-obvious choices that would seem like bugs to a new reader without the explanatory comments.
title: DECISION: incremental migration runner with RAW_MIGRATIONS for FK-toggling DDL
